artists.name: Louis Jordan and His Tympany Five

podcast.title: Characteristics and Influences
podcast.body: Jump band music, pioneered by Louis Jordan and His Tympany Five, was influenced by Lionel Hampton's band and Count Basie. It featured a stripped-back sound compared to big band swing, focusing on simple chord changes (often blues), riffs, solos, and vocals, driven by boogie rhythms and high energy. "The style they were playing in was a style that later became known as jump band music, and it was a style that owed a lot to Lionel Hampton's band and to Count Basie."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Emergence in the 1940s
podcast.body: The jump band style began to gain significant popularity in the 1940s, evolving from the earlier swing music. Lucky Millinder's band was a key proponent, successfully integrating boogie, jump, and jive sounds with a strong blues feeling to create highly danceable music. "Slowly, during the 1940s, Melinda transitioned his band from the kind of swing music that had been popular in the 30s to the jump band style that was becoming more popular."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 7: "Good Rockin' Tonight" by Wynonie Harris

podcast.title: Evolution from Swing
podcast.body: Jump band music was a new type of music rooted in swing, but with a greater emphasis on riffs and amplified instruments. It was pioneered by bands like Lionel Hampton's after he left Benny Goodman's group. "That band would be one of the first bands to perform a new type of music, Jump band music, which was rooted in swing but had more of emphasis on riffs and amplified instruments."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Popularity in Jamaican Sound Systems
podcast.body: Jump band music, along with R&B, was a staple of early Jamaican sound systems, with artists like Louis Jordan being particular favorites. Soundmen relied on finding obscure records from this genre to maintain their competitive edge. "finding more and more obscure old R&B and jump band records."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Precursor to Rhythm and Blues
podcast.body: Jump band music later became known as rhythm and blues. Musicians such as Louis Jordan were explicitly inspired by Lionel Hampton's pioneering jump bands, establishing a clear lineage for the genre. "That Jump band music is the same music that later became known as rhythm and blues, and musicians such as Louis Jordan were clearly inspired by Hampton's band."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Sound and Arrangement
podcast.body: Jump band music, despite being performed by smaller ensembles, achieved a full sound, often with a seemingly complete horn section. Arrangements were stripped back, focusing on punchy delivery and a backbeat, emphasizing vocal personality to convey character typically handled by more instruments in larger bands. "The arrangement is stripped back to the basics to what's necessary, this is a punchy track, and it's a track that makes you want to dance."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
